sources.label: Lok Sabha Starred Q.6, 20.07.2026 (in force 21.11.2025; s.114; Rules notified 08.05.2026)
PIB press note on social security for gig workers

must_be: gig worker or platform worker as defined in the Code

key_facts: First law to define 'gig worker' and 'platform worker'; in force since 21.11.2025
Section 114(1): Government may frame schemes for life & disability cover, accident insurance, health & maternity benefits, old-age protection
Social Security Fund: aggregators contribute 1-2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of amount paid/payable to gig/platform workers
National Social Security Board with aggregator, worker, expert and State representatives
Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026 notified 08.05.2026: mandatory registration of gig/platform workers on the Central Government portal; aggregators must share worker data via API
21 aggregators onboarded on e-Shram incl. Zomato, Blinkit, Swiggy, Ola, Uber, Rapido, Amazon, Porter, Urban Company, Flipkart (as of 20.07.2026)
schemes.status_note: As of 20.07.2026 the s.114 welfare schemes for gig/platform workers are still being formulated; no benefit is claimable under the Code itself yet. UNVERIFIED (secondary source only): date from which aggregator contributions start.
how_to_apply: Nothing to apply for under the Code directly. Register on e-Shram (the portal used for registration).

excluded_or_unverified.reason: NOT a current benefit. The e-Shram ex-gratia (Rs 2 lakh accidental death / disability) only covers workers registered on or before 31 Mar 2022 for incidents on or before 31 Mar 2022 (MoLE guidelines dated 24.08.2023). Some news reports describe it as a current benefit. Do not show it as an active scheme.

No Punjab-government welfare scheme specific to gig or platform workers could be verified on an official page. Punjab Labour Department ran e-Shram registration camps for platform workers from April 2025 (Hindustan Times, 12 Apr 2025, a news source and not official), and 22,272 platform workers in Punjab were registered on e-Shram (Govt reply reported by The Tribune). Do not invent a Punjab scheme. Direct Punjab users to e-Shram.
Real scheme (maandhan.in) but for shopkeepers/self-employed traders, not gig workers; excluded to keep scope tight.
